newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco to sue BankAmerica over bonds.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco to sue BankAmerica over bonds.

text.p: San Francisco plans to file a lawsuit on Thursday against BankAmerica Corp's Bank of America for allegedly overbilling the city, its redevelopment agency, its school district and its housing authority for certain municipal bond services, state sources said.
The San Francisco city attorney's office was expected to announce the lawsuit, which does not allege so-called "yield burning," later on Thursday, the sources said.
The state will not be part of the San Francisco case. California has, however, been conducting its own investigation of Bank of America, the state Attorney General's office said.

"The state has been involved in an investigation with Bank of America for several months," said Rob Stutzman, a spokesman for the state Attorney General. "The state is in the process of mediating the findings of that investigation."
The state's Attorney General office declined to discuss the nature of the state investigation.

But state sources involved in the probe said California's investigation of Bank of America involves alleged overbilling for trustee services and not "yield burning," as was rumored in the municipal bond market.
At issue in the San Francisco and California investigations is Bank of America's institutional trust department, which it sold in 1995, sources said.
That Bank of America department acted as indentured trustee for municipal bonds issued by San Francisco and other California municipalities.
A Bank of America spokesman said he has yet to see San Francisco's lawsuit.
"We've seen rumors of a lawsuit but we have not seen an actual lawsuit," Bank of America spokesman Peter Magnani said.
He said Bank of America has been in negotiations with the city of San Francisco and the state of California "over activities related to a business we no longer own."
Magnani added: "We do not think our exposure in this matter is material."

The $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been rocked by recent charges that bond underwriters overbill issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing transactions, a practice dubbed yield burning.
A spokesman for state Treasurer Matt Fong said the treasurer does not believe alleged yield burning affects the state directly because state bonds are competitively bid.
The San Francisco city attorney's office would not confirm Bank of America was the target of its lawsuit.

The city attorney would only say that the lawsuit involved "fraudulent conduct and claims worth millions of dollars to the city and county of San Francisco, the San Francisco Redevelopment Agency, the San Francisco Unified School District, and the San Francisco Housing Authority."
